questions.question: What is Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW)?

options.text: The total weight of a vehicle and its cargo
The total weight of a vehicle before cargo
The maximum weight allowed to be transported by a vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: The total weight of a vehicle and its cargo
questions.explanation: Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW) means the total weight of the vehicle plus all cargo loaded in it.

questions.question: If a tire fails while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Do not use the brakes. Let the vehicle slow down on its own.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brakes. Let the vehicle slow down on its own.
questions.explanation: When a tire fails, grip the steering wheel firmly. Do not brake. Let the vehicle slow down naturally. Once it has slowed a lot, brake gently and pull off the road safely.

questions.question: Before driving in winter, what should you check?
questions.explanation: Before winter driving, check the heating and defrosting equipment, coolant and antifreeze levels, wipers and washers, tire tread, tire chains, lights, and exhaust system. Clear ice and snow from all windows, mirrors, steps, and the radiator area.

questions.question: If the low air pressure warning light comes on while driving, what does it mean?

options.text: You can only brake if there is enough air in the tanks.
You can brake 14 times before the air runs out.
You can drive normally and check the brakes later.
You can drive but turn on emergency flashers to warn others.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can only brake if there is enough air in the tanks.
questions.explanation: If the low air pressure warning light comes on, stop and park safely as soon as possible. Your brakes will only work as long as there is enough air in the tanks.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what should you use?
questions.explanation: When driving in fog, use your low beam headlights and fog lights, even during the day.

questions.question: If you see a distracted driver on the road, what should you do?
questions.explanation: When you see a distracted driver, give them plenty of space. Be careful when passing because the driver may not see you and could drift into your lane.

questions.question: What do federal and state laws require drivers to do?

options.text: Inspect their vehicles only if they think there may be a problem.
Inspect their vehicles only before traveling out-of-state.
Inspect their vehicles only when transporting hazardous materials.

questions.explanation: Federal and state laws require commercial drivers to inspect their vehicles before every trip. Regular inspections help drivers catch problems before they become dangerous and expensive.

questions.question: When checking brakes, how much should a slack adjuster move?
questions.explanation: Check each slack adjuster by pulling on it. It should not move more than one inch from where it attaches to the push rod. If it moves more than one inch, it needs adjustment.

questions.question: How can you check if a trailer has ABS?

options.text: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensor wires from the brakes.
Look under the hood for an ABS sticker.
Remove a tire and look for the sensor on the axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensor wires from the brakes.
questions.explanation: To check if a trailer has ABS, look underneath for the electronic control unit and wheel speed sensor wires connected to the back of the brakes.

questions.question: Which person should motorists NOT worry about as a distraction?

options.text: A driver talking to another person in the vehicle
Children on the side of the road
Construction workers on the side of the road
A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus

questions.correctAnswerText: A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
questions.explanation: Drivers talking to passengers may not pay full attention to the road. Children may run into the street without looking. Be careful around construction workers. A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus is not a distraction concern.

questions.question: How should cargo inside a trailer be handled?

options.text: It does not need to be secured.
It should be stacked no higher than three feet.
It should be secured so it does not move.
It should have the heaviest items on top of lighter items.

questions.correctAnswerText: It should be secured so it does not move.
questions.explanation: Cargo must be secured to prevent it from moving during transit. Load cargo to keep the vehicle's center of gravity low and evenly distributed.

questions.question: What must you provide to get a hazardous materials endorsement?

options.text: A list of countries you visited in the last 10 years.
Your work history for the last five years.

questions.explanation: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, you must submit your fingerprints and pass a TSA background check.

questions.question: How can you prevent a manual transmission vehicle from rolling backward when starting?

options.text: Partly engage the clutch before you lift your foot off the brake.
Put the vehicle in reverse before moving forward.
Fully engage the clutch before you lift your foot off the brake.
Put the vehicle in neutral before moving forward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Partly engage the clutch before you lift your foot off the brake.
questions.explanation: To prevent rolling backward, partly engage the clutch before you lift your foot off the brake. Use the parking brake when needed to keep your vehicle from rolling back.

questions.question: What happens if you press and release the brake pedal unnecessarily?

options.text: Air is released faster than the system can replace it.
More air is added to the braking system.
The brake pedal becomes more sensitive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air is released faster than the system can replace it.
questions.explanation: In an air brake system, pressing and releasing the brake pedal unnecessarily releases air faster than the compressor can replace it.

questions.question: What two things tell you when to shift to a higher gear?

options.text: Oil pressure and air brake pressure.

questions.explanation: The two indicators for upshifting are engine speed (rpm) and road speed (mph). Check your vehicle's manual to learn the correct rpm range for each gear. Watch your speedometer and shift up when you reach the appropriate speed.

questions.question: What happens to a vehicle's speed when going downhill?

options.text: It matches the speed of traffic.

questions.explanation: Gravity causes a vehicle's speed to increase when going downhill. Before going downhill, choose a safe speed based on your vehicle's size and weight.

questions.question: What should drivers do with a front brake limiting valve to maintain normal stopping power?

options.text: Set the control to the off position.
Keep the control at the halfway mark.

questions.explanation: Some older vehicles have a front brake limiting valve with "normal" and "slippery" settings. These valves do not actually help prevent front-wheel skids. Always leave the valve in the "normal" position.

questions.question: When should you test the low pressure warning signal?
questions.explanation: Your low pressure warning light is very important. After the system charges, test it by quickly pressing and releasing the brake pedal several times. The warning signal should come on when pressure drops to a dangerous level.

questions.question: What should you NOT do during an engine fire?

options.text: Turn the engine off as soon as possible.
Spray foam from under the vehicle.

questions.explanation: During an engine fire, turn the engine off immediately. Do not open the hood if you can avoid it. Spray foam through the louvers or from under the vehicle.

questions.question: What happens when only the tractor has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS)?

options.text: The brakes do not work as well as without ABS.

questions.explanation: When only the tractor has ABS but the trailer does not, the risk of jackknifing is reduced and you can still steer the vehicle. If only the trailer has ABS, the trailer is less likely to swing to one side.

questions.question: What is a wig wag?

options.text: A tube used to move air from the compressor to the tanks
A noise made by air brakes when used
A part within the braking unit that allows air to move freely

questions.explanation: A wig wag is a low air pressure warning device. It drops a mechanical arm into your view when air pressure in the tanks falls below 60 psi.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, belts in the engine compartment should be:

options.text: Inspected only if they seem frayed.

questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, check belts for tightness and wear.

questions.question: When driving through a curve during the skills test, you should:

options.text: Veer from your lane if needed to complete the curve.
Reduce your speed after entering the curve.
Refrain from looking for other vehicles while turning.
Reduce your speed before entering the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed before entering the curve.
questions.explanation: Slow down before you enter a curve. Do this so you don't need to brake or shift while turning. Stay in your lane and watch for other traffic.

questions.question: If something is found to be unsafe during a pre-trip inspection, you should:

options.text: Continue with the trip and make an appointment with a mechanic after the trip is completed.
Let a more experienced driver use the truck.
Not use the items found to be unsafe, but may continue driving normally.

questions.explanation: If a pre-trip inspection finds something unsafe, you must repair it right away. It is illegal to drive an unsafe vehicle.

questions.question: Mirrors should be adjusted:

options.text: When you are standing next to the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Check mirrors before you start your trip. If your vehicle has a trailer, you can only adjust mirrors correctly when the trailer is straight.

questions.question: When using your mirrors, you should frequently look at your tires to:

options.text: See if the tires are rolling properly.
See if the tread is sufficient.
Get a sense of the size of the tire in relation to other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Check your tires often in your mirrors to notice tire fires. Fires can happen when tires are under-inflated, when dual tires touch, or when tires overheat.

questions.question: How could you reduce your stress while driving?
questions.explanation: Stress can lead to aggressive and dangerous driving. Calming music can help you relax while driving.

questions.question: If coolant has to be added to a system without a recovery tank, you should:

options.text: Keep the vehicle running while adding coolant.
Not use gloves to touch the radiator cap.
Wait for the engine to cool before adding coolant.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the engine to cool before adding coolant.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine and let it cool before adding coolant. Use gloves or a thick cloth to protect your hands. Turn the radiator cap slowly to the first stop to release pressure.

questions.question: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS):

options.text: Are equipped in addition to other braking systems and do not reduce normal braking power.
Are not effective on larger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are equipped in addition to other braking systems and do not reduce normal braking power.
questions.explanation: ABS works with your normal braking system. It does not increase or decrease your braking power. ABS activates during hard braking to prevent wheels from locking up.

questions.question: A high center of gravity:

options.text: Makes a vehicle more susceptible to rollover.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes a vehicle more susceptible to rollover.
questions.explanation: A high center of gravity makes a vehicle more likely to tip over.

questions.question: What happens when driving in extremely hot weather?

options.text: You need to remove oil from the engine.
It is safer to use less coolant.

questions.explanation: Hot weather causes air inside tires to expand, which increases tire pressure to dangerous levels. Keep enough oil and coolant in your engine to prevent overheating.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sign of drowsiness?
questions.explanation: Warning signs of drowsiness include blinking a lot, eyes closing or losing focus by themselves, frequent yawning, and drifting between lanes. Always avoid drowsy driving.

questions.question: What can a modulating control valve control?
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets a driver apply spring brakes gradually. In vehicles with this system, a lever on the dashboard controls the valve.

questions.question: How can you fix a skid caused by acceleration?

options.text: Remove your foot from the accelerator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove your foot from the accelerator.
questions.explanation: Remove your foot from the accelerator to fix a skid caused by acceleration. On very slippery surfaces, you may also need to push in the clutch.

questions.question: Where is the tire load rating located?

options.text: On the inside of the driver's door
On the side of each tire

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side of each tire
questions.explanation: The tire load rating is the maximum weight a tire can safely carry at a certain pressure. This number is printed on the side of each tire.

questions.question: Why is a stopped bus a concern?

options.text: It is only a concern if passengers are getting off.
It should never be on the road.
It is a concern whether you see passengers or not.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is a concern whether you see passengers or not.
questions.explanation: Always drive carefully around stopped buses. Passengers may cross in front or behind the bus. The bus may block their view of your vehicle.

questions.question: What is the best way to check your lights during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Park near a mirror to see a reflection
Turn on the lights, then get out to look at them
Check the instrument panel for warning lights
Drive in traffic and wait for other drivers to tell you if lights are out

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on the lights, then get out to look at them
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, turn on your lights and then exit your vehicle to check that they work.

questions.question: During the skills test, if you must stop before making a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Stop after the stop line for a better view.
Keep the front wheels pointed straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the front wheels pointed straight ahead.
questions.explanation: Come to a smooth stop behind any stop line, crosswalk, or stop sign. Keep your front wheels pointed straight and do not let your vehicle roll. If stopping behind another vehicle, stop where you can still see its rear tires.

questions.question: How many times can you exit your vehicle to check its position during backing exercises (not straight line backing)?
questions.explanation: You can exit your vehicle to check its position during basic control skills tests. This is called a "look." During straight line backing, you may look only once. During other exercises, you may look up to two times.

questions.question: What should you do when transporting cargo?

options.text: Check the load and securing devices within the first 50 miles.
Hold your cell phone in case of emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the load and securing devices within the first 50 miles.
questions.explanation: Inspect cargo and securing devices before you start driving. After starting your trip, check them within the first 50 miles, every 3 hours or 150 miles, and after every break.

questions.question: When braking at 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about ____ to your total stopping distance.
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to your stopping distance.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a distraction while driving?
questions.explanation: Anything that takes your attention away from driving is a dangerous distraction. This includes eating, drinking, smoking, and adjusting audio or climate controls. Checking mirrors is part of safe driving.

questions.question: What is one way to manage blind spots?

options.text: Drive faster than other vehicles so no one can pass you.
Drive in the left lane so you only worry about vehicles on your right.
Check your mirrors often and know where other vehicles are around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors often and know where other vehicles are around you.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors frequently to watch the traffic around you. This helps you notice if other vehicles are moving into your blind spots.

questions.question: In an emergency, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Stopping is not always the safest choice in an emergency. It is usually safer to steer away from danger to avoid a crash.

questions.question: What should you do with a burning tire?
questions.explanation: Cool a burning tire with water. You may need to use a large amount of water to cool it properly.

questions.question: Where is the safety relief valve usually located?
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve in an air brake system is located in the tank that receives air first from the compressor.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a distracted person that drivers should worry about?

options.text: A driver talking to a passenger in their vehicle
A child on the side of the road
A construction worker on the side of the road
A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus

questions.correctAnswerText: A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
questions.explanation: Be careful around people who are not paying attention to traffic. Watch out for road workers, drivers talking with passengers, and children near the road. A person waiting on a bench is not a traffic concern.

questions.question: What does the suspension system do?

options.text: Holds up the vehicle and its load.
Keeps the load the proper distance behind the driver's compartment.
Maintains a safe distance between the vehicle and other vehicles.
Lightens the load for the tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Holds up the vehicle and its load.
questions.explanation: The suspension system holds up the vehicle and its load while keeping the axles in place. A damaged suspension system can be very dangerous.

questions.question: If another driver is tailgating you, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Increase your distance from the vehicle in front of you.
Avoid using tricks to help others pass.

questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, increase your following distance, avoid quick moves, and do not use tricks like flashing lights. Speeding up will not help—it will only make the tailgater follow you faster and increase danger.

questions.question: When approaching a curve during the driving test, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Slow down before entering the curve.
Keep your vehicle in its lane.
Use the brakes steadily throughout the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the brakes steadily throughout the curve.
questions.explanation: When approaching a curve, check traffic in all directions. Slow down before entering the curve so you do not need to brake or shift while turning. Stay in your lane and keep checking traffic. Do not brake while in the curve.
